title: feat(rpc): implement a live HTTP transport over the official client
problem: `devkit-rpc` defines a `Transport` trait and a mock, but there is no transport that actually talks to a Stellar RPC node.
why: Without a live transport the toolkit cannot perform real RPC-based workflows, which is a core part of the product.
context: The official `stellar-rpc-client` crate (28.0.0-rc.1) exists; integrate it rather than writing a JSON-RPC client from scratch.
scope: Implement a `Transport` backed by `stellar-rpc-client`, behind a non-default feature if it adds heavy dependencies.
Map transport errors into `DevkitError` without panicking.
out_of_scope: New RPC methods beyond those already modeled.
guidance: Study the `stellar-rpc-client` API before implementing; adapt it to the `Transport` trait.
Keep the mock transport the default in tests; the live transport must be opt-in.
acceptance: A live transport can call `getHealth` against a configured endpoint
Errors are structured and non-panicking
tests: Unit tests with a recorded/loopback server where feasible
A test asserting the transport is not used by default
security: The transport must only use validated `Endpoint`s and must not log credentials.
performance: Reuse a single connection pool where the client allows it.
docs: Document supported methods and the fact that live RPC is opt-in.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(rpc): add timeouts and cancellation to RPC calls
problem: RPC calls have no timeout, so a slow or hanging endpoint can block a command indefinitely.
why: Bounded calls are required for safe, predictable tooling and for CI.
context: The transport abstraction is in place; the policy belongs at the client layer.
scope: Add configurable connect/read timeouts to the RPC client
Fail with a clear error when the budget is exceeded
guidance: Keep timeouts configurable and default to a conservative value.
acceptance: A timeout produces a structured error
The default timeout is documented
tests: Unit test with a mock that exceeds the budget
security: Timeouts reduce denial-of-service risk from untrusted endpoints.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(rpc): add exponential backoff with jitter to retries
problem: The retry policy retries immediately, which can hammer a struggling endpoint.
why: Backoff with jitter is standard practice for resilient clients.
context: `RetryPolicy` exists and only retries transport failures.
scope: Add a backoff strategy with configurable base and cap
Add jitter to avoid thundering herds
guidance: Keep the delay injectable so tests do not sleep.
acceptance: Backoff is applied between retries
Tests do not sleep
tests: Unit test asserting the computed delay sequence
security: Reduce load amplification against untrusted endpoints.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(rpc): add a typed model for getLedgerEntries
problem: `getLedgerEntries` is not modeled, so callers receive raw JSON.
why: Typed ledger entries are needed for contract storage inspection.
context: The RPC reference documents `getLedgerEntries` with base64 XDR keys and entries.
scope: Add request/response types
Decode entry XDR into a developer-friendly shape
acceptance: Typed entries parse from recorded fixtures
Malformed entries are structured errors
security: Bound decoding of untrusted entry XDR.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(rpc): add typed models for getTransaction and getTransactions
why: Typed transactions enable envelope, result, and event analysis.
context: `getTransaction` returns status, envelope XDR, result XDR, and meta XDR.
scope: Model the response and decode envelope/result XDR where present
Represent `NOT_FOUND` explicitly
guidance: Separate confirmed fields from optional ones.
acceptance: Typed transaction parses from a fixture
NOT_FOUND is a distinct, non-error outcome
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(rpc): add a typed model for getFeeStats
why: Typed fee statistics support developer tooling around fees.
context: The RPC reference documents inclusion and Soroban inclusion fee distributions.
scope: Model the fee distribution fields
Ignore unknown fields
guidance: Make percentile fields optional to tolerate schema changes.
acceptance: Typed fee stats parse from a fixture
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(core): add a configuration system with file and environment support
problem: There is no configuration system; networks, endpoints, and output settings cannot be persisted.
why: Configuration is required for real workflows and CI.
scope: Load configuration from a TOML file and `STELLAR_FOUNDRY_*` environment variables.
Validate unknown fields and referenced values.
guidance: Treat configuration files as untrusted input; never let them enable network access implicitly.
acceptance: Config precedence is documented and tested
Invalid config is rejected with a clear error
security: Configuration must never contain or log secrets; document this.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(config): resolve network profiles and custom endpoints
problem: Networks are modeled but there is no resolution of an effective endpoint per network.
why: Users need to select a network and have the right endpoint and passphrase applied consistently.
context: Mainnet has no default endpoint by design.
scope: Resolve an effective endpoint from config + CLI flags
Validate it with `Endpoint::parse`
guidance: Fail closed when no endpoint is configured for mainnet.
acceptance: Endpoint resolution is deterministic and tested
tests: Unit tests for each network and overrides
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(cli): add live RPC diagnostics to doctor
problem: `doctor` reports capabilities but cannot check a live endpoint.
why: Connectivity diagnostics are one of the first things developers need.
scope: Add `doctor --rpc <URL>` that checks health and network, with a clear opt-in
Never perform network access without the flag
guidance: Reuse the RPC client and validated endpoints.
acceptance: No network access without the flag
Clear diagnostics on failure
security: Opt-in only; document the network policy.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(core): add structured logging with levels
problem: There is no logging; debugging requires ad-hoc prints.
why: Leveled logs on stderr improve supportability without polluting machine output.
scope: Add `--log-level` writing structured logs to stderr
Never log secrets or source content
acceptance: Log level is configurable and tested
Default output unchanged
tests: CLI test asserting stderr logging and clean stdout
security: Never log credentials or full URLs with userinfo.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.

title: feat(scval): add curated human-readable rendering for common SCVal types
problem: Decoded SCVal JSON mirrors the XDR shape, which is verbose and hard to read.
why: Readable output is the main value of an inspection tool.
context: The JSON shape is currently unstable by design.
scope: Render booleans, integers, timestamps, strings, symbols, bytes, addresses, vectors, and maps
Fall back to the raw JSON for unknown variants
guidance: Never present inference as fact; label unknown variants explicitly.
acceptance: Each documented variant has a rendering
Unknown variants are handled without panic
tests: Unit tests per variant plus an unknown-variant test
security: Bound the size of rendered output.
performance: Rendering is linear in value size.
dod: Merged with tests passing and CI green.
